title: Heart and stomach fibres stay geodetic after the twisting of the primitive tube

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Heart and stomach fibres stay geodetic after the twisting of the primitive tube

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The heart and stomach develop from simple tubes by dilatation and twisting; their originally circular and longitudinal fibres remain geodetic on the distorted surface, new geodetic systems (such as the oblique stomach fibres) appear on new pouches, and the heart contracts effectively only because its fibres run the shortest course.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. X: A Parenthetic Note on Geodetics

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: these systems of muscular fibres, geodetic to begin with, remain geodetic (in the sense in which we are using the word) after all the twisting to which the primitive cylindrical tube or tubes have been subjected.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter X, “A Parenthetic Note on Geodetics”; topic “Geodetics of heart and stomach”. Scope: vertebrate (especially mammalian) heart and stomach musculature

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch10-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Parts of the geometry can be tested in developmental atlases, but 'remain geodetic' requires longitudinal correspondence rarely present. Efficiency and persistence claims have multiple developmental and biomechanical rivals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Register embryonic heart and stomach tube stages to later organ surfaces, track fibre lineages, and test whether trajectories remain geodesic after deformation and whether shorter paths predict contraction efficiency. Compare with active fibre-remodeling models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fibres differentiate and remodel during organogenesis rather than simply deforming passively.

Lineage-resolved fibre tracking across twisting stages is uncommon.

fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.5

discriminating power: 0.4

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The adult heart can be checked for geodesic fibers, which is only the end state of a developmental claim about dilatation, twisting and new gastric systems. Open data are adult ventricular diffusion and shape, not a series from the primitive tube and not a comparable stomach dataset. The further claim that the heart works only because fibers take the shortest course is not separated from other working architectures by these measurements.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether adult heart and stomach fibers are geodesics of the twisted surface, whether oblique gastric fibers match a new pouch geodesic, and whether pump performance requires that shortest-path layout. Adult geodesic fits support only the geometric residue of the developmental claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Remaining geodetic after twisting requires the fiber map through development, which these adult datasets do not contain.

Effective contraction is compatible with non-geodesic architectures, so function does not isolate the shortest path as necessary.
